title: B2 · L2 — Mixed conditionals
description: Condicionales mixtos: combinan tiempos entre condición y resultado para expresar hipótesis complejas entre pasado y presente.

questions.prompt: Situación: comentas con un colega la trayectoria de una compañera bilingüe.
questions.question: Complete: 'If she ___ Spanish at school, she ___ this job now.'
options: studied / would have
had studied / would have
studied / would have had
had studied / had
questions.explanation: Este es el mixto clásico past→present: 'had studied' (algo que no ocurrió en el pasado) + 'would have' (consecuencia en el PRESENTE, aquí 'now'). El detonante visual es la palabra 'now'. Error típico de hispanohablante: usar el tercer condicional puro ('would have HAD') pensando en 'habría tenido', pero la consecuencia sigue viva hoy, no es pasada.
examples: If I had learned to code back in college, I'd have a much better salary now. → charla de café
If they had invested in Bitcoin in 2013, they'd be millionaires today.

questions.prompt: Situación: te disculpas por haber olvidado un cumpleaños.
questions.question: Which sentence is a present→past mixed conditional?
options: If I had money, I would buy it.
If I were more organised, I wouldn't have forgotten your birthday.
If I had had money, I would have bought it.
If I have money, I will buy it.
questions.explanation: El mixto present→past usa 'were/had (presente)' en la condición + 'would have + participio' en el resultado. Un rasgo PERMANENTE de carácter (ser desorganizado) explica un fallo puntual del pasado. Las otras opciones son segundo condicional (A), tercero puro (C) o primero (D).
examples: If she weren't so shy, she would've spoken up in yesterday's meeting. → cotilleo de oficina
If he weren't allergic to shellfish, he would've tried the paella at the wedding.

questions.statement: Los condicionales mixtos solo combinan marcos temporales pasado y presente.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO en el uso estándar. Los mixtos canónicos son 'past→present' (condición pasada, resultado actual) y 'present→past' (condición estable, resultado pasado). Combinaciones con futuro existen técnicamente pero suenan forzadas y rara vez las oirás en inglés natural, incluso entre nativos cultos.
examples: Past→present: If I hadn't eaten that dodgy sushi, I wouldn't feel so awful now.
Present→past: If I were braver, I would've asked her out at the party last week.

questions.text: If I hadn't taken that flight, I wouldn't be here talking to you now.
questions.explanation: Frase de storytelling emocional (una boda, una charla TED). Connected speech: 'hadn't' pierde la /t/ final antes de consonante → 'hadn(t) taken'. 'Wouldn't be' se fusiona como 'wouldn(t) bi'. El adverbio 'now' al final es el marcador clave que revela que es mixto past→present, no tercer condicional puro.
examples: If I hadn't quit that toxic job, I wouldn't be this happy today. → confesión honesta
If we hadn't moved to Lisbon, we wouldn't be raising our kids by the sea.

questions.prompt: Un padre habla de su hijo con la profesora.
questions.question: Complete: 'If he ___ so lazy, he ___ his exams last year.'
options: weren't / would pass
hadn't been / would pass
weren't / would have passed
wasn't being / will pass
questions.explanation: Present→past mixed. 'Weren't' se refiere a un rasgo que sigue vigente (sigue siendo perezoso), y 'would have passed' apunta a un resultado pasado concreto (los exámenes del año pasado). Nota que en registro cuidado usamos 'were' para todas las personas en condicionales, aunque en hablado 'was' es aceptable.
examples: If she weren't so proud, she would've apologised to her sister ages ago.
If I weren't such a deep sleeper, I would've heard the smoke alarm last night.

questions.prompt: Empareja cada condición mixta con su resultado lógico:

pairs.left: If I hadn't missed the bus,
pairs.right: I would be at work now.
she would have finished the puzzle.

pairs.left: If he weren't afraid of flying,
pairs.right: he would have visited Japan by now.

pairs.left: If I had accepted the offer,
pairs.right: I would be living in Berlin.

questions.explanation: Cada par mezcla dos marcos temporales. Truco para identificar el tipo: busca adverbios reveladores — 'now', 'still', 'today', 'by now' señalan que el resultado es presente; sin ellos, probablemente sea pasado. La cláusula 'if' te dice si la condición es pasada ('had done') o presente ('were').
examples: If I had studied linguistics, I'd speak French fluently now. → past→present
If she weren't so bossy, no one would've quit the team last month. → present→past

questions.statement: En 'If I were richer, I would have bought that house last year', 'were' se refiere a un estado presente general.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Were' aquí describe una realidad ESTABLE actual (no soy rico), aplicada a una decisión pasada concreta (no compré la casa). Si dijéramos 'If I HAD BEEN richer last year, I would have bought it', el foco sería sólo aquel momento pasado — matiz distinto.
examples: If I were taller, I would've made the basketball team back in school.
If she were more confident, she would've said yes to the promotion last month.

questions.prompt: Escribes un mensaje a tu equipo explicando por qué faltas a la daily.
questions.question: Which sentence best fits after: 'I overslept this morning.'?
options: If I hadn't overslept, I would be at the meeting now.
If I don't oversleep, I would be at the meeting.
If I overslept, I will miss the meeting.
If I hadn't overslept, I would have been at the meeting now.
questions.explanation: Past→present clásico: la acción pasada ('overslept') afecta el ahora ('the meeting now'). La opción D mezcla mal 'would have been' con 'now' — si la reunión sigue ocurriendo, el resultado es presente ('would be'), no pasado. Error muy común: sobrecorregir y meter 'would have' donde no toca.
examples: If I hadn't eaten that dodgy taco last night, I wouldn't feel sick now. → excusa por trabajar desde casa
If they had left at 6, they'd be here by now — something must've happened.

questions.target: If I had accepted that scholarship, I would probably be working in Silicon Valley now.
questions.explanation: Reflexión típica de entrevista o charla honesta con un mentor. Nota que 'probably' se coloca ENTRE el modal ('would') y el auxiliar ('be'), no al final — es el orden natural del inglés. Nativos suavizan aún más con 'I guess', 'maybe' o 'who knows' al final para no sonar demasiado seguros del hipotético.
examples: Honestly, if I'd moved to New York after college, I'd probably be a struggling artist by now.
If she had studied law, she'd be a partner at some big firm by now — but she seems happier this way.

questions.prompt: Tu jefe da feedback a un empleado sobre el trimestre pasado.
questions.question: Complete: 'If you ___ more organised, you ___ the deadline last week.'
options: were / would meet
had been / would have met
were / would have met
are / would meet
questions.explanation: Present→past mixed. 'Were more organised' describe un rasgo actual (crítica al carácter, no a un momento puntual); 'would have met' señala la consecuencia pasada perdida. Nativos suavizan esta crítica con hedging: 'Maybe if you were a bit more organised...' para que no suene agresivo.
examples: If you were less impulsive, you wouldn't have sent that email to the whole company.
Look, if she were a bit more careful, she wouldn't have broken the client's prototype. → feedback franco

questions.statement: Los condicionales mixtos se usan principalmente para especular sobre consecuencias futuras.
questions.explanation: FALSO. Los mixtos conectan pasado con presente (o al revés); para el futuro se usan primer condicional (real) o segundo condicional (hipotético). Meter futuro en un mixto suena raro y suele indicar que en realidad querías otro tipo de condicional.
examples: Past→present: If I had saved more in my 20s, I'd have a house deposit now.
Present→past: If I weren't such a people-pleaser, I would've said no to that extra project.

questions.text: If we weren't so busy at work, we would have visited you last summer.
questions.explanation: Present→past en un contexto de disculpa amistosa. Weak forms: 'we weren't' se pronuncia relajado como 'wi-wɜːnt', y 'would have' colapsa a 'would've'. Nota que 'so busy' recibe el énfasis prosódico — es la palabra emocional que justifica la disculpa.
examples: If we weren't drowning in deadlines, we would've come to your wedding.
If I weren't such a workaholic, I would've taken proper holidays this year. → autoconfesión

questions.prompt: Un asistente social describe la trayectoria de una usuaria.
questions.question: Which sentence best expresses: 'She still lives in poverty because she didn't finish university'?
options: If she finished university, she wouldn't be poor.
If she had finished university, she wouldn't have been poor.
If she had finished university, she wouldn't be living in poverty.
If she finishes university, she won't be poor.
questions.explanation: Past→present con present continuous en el resultado ('wouldn't be living') para enfatizar la situación actual, persistente y visible. La opción B (tercer condicional puro) sugeriría que la pobreza fue algo puntual pasado ya superado, lo cual contradice el 'still lives'.
examples: If he had listened to his mentor, he wouldn't be dealing with this mess now.
If they had planned their finances better, they wouldn't be struggling with debt today.

questions.target: If I weren't so afraid of change, I would have taken that job in Tokyo last year.
questions.explanation: Confesión personal muy típica en terapia, coaching o charla profunda con un amigo. El énfasis natural cae en 'so afraid' — la palabra emocional. Nativos añaden pausas ('...you know...') o hedging ('honestly', 'I guess') para suavizar la autocrítica sin quitarle sinceridad.
examples: Honestly, if I weren't such a cautious investor, I would've bought Tesla shares five years ago.
You know, if he weren't so proud, he would've accepted help months ago — and he'd be in a better place now.

questions.prompt: Estás redactando la introducción de una novela.
questions.question: Choose the correct inversion for a past→present mixed conditional (formal/literary):
options: Had I been born in Italy, I would speak Italian fluently.
If had I been born in Italy, I would speak Italian.
Were I born in Italy, I would have spoken Italian.
Had I born in Italy, I would speak Italian.
questions.explanation: La inversión formal invierte el auxiliar y omite 'if': 'Had I been born...'. Es registro literario o retórico — puro artificio elegante. En un chat casual dirías 'If I'd been born in Italy...'. Nota que en la opción D falta el 'been' — 'had born' es agramatical porque 'born' es participio pasivo y necesita 'been'.
examples: Had I studied law instead of literature, I would be a judge today. → prólogo de memorias
Had she accepted his proposal that summer, she would be married with three kids by now.
